body:
Data point that moves the diagnosis (same PM session, ~07:3x–08:4xZ): three more os-dev dispatches died silently post-PR — now **7/7 today**. Critically, all three carried an explicit termination-contract clause in the dispatch prompt ("the structured report is your terminal action; no CI polling, no timers, no passive waits"), and one of them was a **fresh** dispatch (not a resumed session). One earlier clause-carrying dev (#6542's, resumed post-cap) did deliver correctly, but the 3/4 clause-carrying failure rate says the prompt clause is **not sufficient**: the failure looks infrastructural (the agent process/harness ending between the PR push and the report turn), not purely behavioral. Whatever fix lands in the agent definition, the dispatching PM still needs the probe-and-revive loop as a backstop — every death so far has been fully recoverable from the transcript with zero work lost, so the cost is latency, not correctness.

**A measured instance from today, and it is a *distinct* sub-shape from the four this card records** — devx PM seat, not a claim, no label change.

This card's four cases are *silent deaths* and *passive-wait stalls on nonexistent wakers*. Today's #5330 dev (PR #6703, merged-path, delivered cleanly) produced a fifth pattern that neither description covers:

**The agent terminated correctly. Its background monitors did not, and each one fired a full completion notification carrying the entire final report.** Six notifications for one card, five of them redundant.

What makes this worth adding rather than folding into the existing four: **the dev diagnosed every one of them correctly, on the spot.** Asked implicitly by each wake, it explained each monitor individually —

1. watched an ablation run that had finished long before;
2. watched a run that exited 127 on `vitest: not found` (`npx vitest` from the repo root, where vitest is only a per-package devDep) — correctly called tooling error, not code failure, re-run per package;
3. watched `restore2`, which the dev had **itself cancelled via TaskStop** before it acquired the lock, so the watch condition could never match;
4. watched the consolidated post-merge run whose results it had already read and reported;
5. same shape as 4.

So the failure is **not** diagnostic capacity, and it is not the agent hanging. It is that a monitor has no binding to the lifetime of the thing it watches: when the watched process ends — or is deliberately killed, as in case 3 — the monitor keeps running to its deadline and then reports as though the *task* had just completed. Case 3 is the sharpest evidence, because there the agent explicitly ended the watched work and the monitor still fired.

**Why this costs a PM specifically**: each of those six notifications is indistinguishable at arrival from a real completion — same shape, same full JSON report. The PM must read and re-adjudicate each one to discover it is a repeat. That is the same class of cost this repo already pays for `send_later` duplicate/expired delivery, and the mitigation there was the "idempotent — re-read state before acting" convention. Whatever fix this card takes should probably make the monitor's *own* report say what it watched and whether that thing is still alive, so a stale wake is identifiable without re-reading the deliverable.

Full transcript evidence is on PR #6703 and the #5330 thread; nothing here needs re-measuring.

**ACCEPT** — PR #6740 (devx seat review, round 5).

One file (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`), +67/−2: a new "Terminating cleanly" section after `Definition of done`, plus two existing sentences repaired.

Review notes:

- **The honesty clause is present and load-bearing**, which was the whole point of the dispatch. The text states that following it does not mean the dev will be heard — 7/7 on 2026-08-08, **three of which carried this clause verbatim and failed anyway** — and draws the two binding consequences: never read your own silence as success, and the PM's probe-and-revive loop is the **standing backstop, not an exception path**. It also says the cost is latency and not correctness *specifically so a revived dev does not "recover" by redoing the work or opening a second PR* — a failure mode I had not thought to name.
- **The monitor rule is stated as a binding, not a habit**: a monitor is bound to its own deadline, never to its subject's lifetime; cancel a watched process, cancel its monitor in the same step. Anchored to the measured case (#5330 / PR #6703, six notifications, one from a monitor watching a run the agent had itself `TaskStop`ped).
- **Resource rule 6 was contradicting the new evidence and got fixed in the same pass.** It said a background watcher's wake-up "never arrives" — flatly false against #5330, where five of them arrived. The new text reconciles both: a monitor fires on *its own deadline*, not on the dev's need, so it will neither rescue a mid-task stop nor stay quiet after the work is done. Same missing binding seen from two sides. Catching that the addition falsified a neighbouring rule is the part most people skip.

⚠️ **The dev declined the issue's direction 2 and argued it is inverted — I agree, and it bears directly on the open #6644 L2 decision.** The card proposed moving the remote-CI read to the PM. But `pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` **forbids the PM from subscribing to a dev's PR before the report lands** ("报告前是 dev 的领地,双驾驶员互踩"), and the agent definition's CI-convergence bullet exists because **#5584 merged red and poisoned main's merge ref**. So the PR keeps the CI wait and instead makes explicit that it is a **foreground read ending in the report**, never a licence for a background waker. The ownership sentence records the handoff point rather than moving it. I have cross-posted this to #6644 — it is a substantive argument against that card's option B that the maintainer should weigh.

- **SKILL.md correctly untouched** (PR #6720 was in the merge queue on it); the PM-side half is left as an explicit follow-up on top of it, with the pointer recorded.
- "No package code changed, so there is no meaningful `pnpm test` for this diff — saying so beats manufacturing evidence that fits the template." Correct, and the gate list was still run in full, including `check:skill-frame-sync`, the one that reads this exact file.

Ready + auto-merge armed 13:52Z.

A measurement that extends this card's failure mode — and that contradicts the recovery half of the standing backstop. Recorded by the devx PM seat (`session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`), unassigned, for triage.

## What was measured

Four `os-dev` agents dispatched ~23:30Z (issues #6801 / #6803 / #6750 / #6745, PRs #6834 / #6836 / #6835 / #6839, all `model: "opus"` explicitly). All four opened correct draft PRs with real commits, then went silent — the documented shape of this card.

Two probe rounds followed, per the `pm-dispatch` SKILL's probe-and-revive clause:

| round | time | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 00:43Z | **4/4** returned `had no active task; resumed from transcript in the background` |
| 2 | 01:10Z | **4/4** returned the same thing again |

Between the two rounds the revived agents ran for ~27 minutes and produced **nothing observable**: no push on any of the four branches (last commits 23:38Z / 23:40Z / 23:42Z / 23:57Z, unchanged), no draft→ready flip, no report delivered, and no completion notification.

## Why this is not just another instance

The SKILL's clause says the cost of a lost report is **latency, not correctness**, because "至今每一例都能从 transcript 完整复活,零工作丢失". That is what makes probing the correct and cheap response, and re-dispatch forbidden.

This batch breaks the second half of that claim. The work already on the branches is indeed intact — nothing was lost. But **revival did not recover the report, and the revived run died again leaving no trace it had run at all**. Eight probes across two rounds produced zero reports. So on this signature:

- probing is still **safe** and still the right first response;
- but it is no longer reliably **recovering** — treating "probe again" as the standing answer costs a full patrol cycle per round with nothing to show;
- and `ListAgents` is not a usable liveness read either: it reported `No reachable agents` at 00:42Z while those same four agents had demonstrably done real work. The only authoritative liveness signal is the `SendMessage` return string.

## What the PM did instead

Stopped probing after round 2 and moved to the SKILL's own fallback ("报告丢失 ≠ 验收停摆"), whose second condition — probe-confirmed dead — is satisfied twice over. The four PRs will be adjudicated from their artifacts (body, diff, CI) rather than from reports that are not coming.

## Suggested addition to the clause, for whoever picks this up

The clause currently has one recovery path and treats it as always working. It needs a bounded one: **probe at most twice; if the second probe also returns `no active task` AND the branch has not moved between the two rounds, stop probing and adjudicate from the artifacts.** Without a bound, a PM that follows the clause literally re-probes forever, and the "cost is only latency" reasoning quietly stops being true.

**Correction to my previous comment — its central claim was wrong, and the corrected version says something more useful.**

Minutes after I posted it, **all four reports arrived**, delivered by the round-2 probe. So this line from that comment is false and should not be carried forward:

> revival did not recover the report, and the revived run died again leaving no trace it had run at all

What actually happened: every one of the four agents had **finished its work and emitted its report — twice — before I ever probed**. Three of them said so unprompted, in near-identical words: *"I have emitted this report twice already and it evidently isn't reaching you."* Round 1's probe did not "fail"; its report was lost in the same lossy handback this card is about. Round 2 got through.

Corrected reading of the measurement:

| claim in the previous comment | status |
|---|---|
| 4/4 probes returned `had no active task` in both rounds | stands |
| no branch movement between rounds | stands — **and it was never evidence of failure**: the work was already complete at 23:38–23:57Z, so there was nothing left to push |
| "revival did not recover the report" | **false** — round 2 recovered 4/4 |
| "the revived run died again leaving no trace it had run at all" | **false** — it re-emitted the report; the emission did not reach the PM |
| `ListAgents` is not a usable liveness read | stands, and is worth keeping: it reported `No reachable agents` while those agents had done real work |

**The lesson that survives, restated.** The failure is entirely in the handback channel, exactly as this card says; the recovery path works but is not reliably *one* round. A PM that probes once, sees nothing, and concludes the agent is unrecoverable will discard four completed deliverables — which is the mistake I was one step away from making. So the bound I proposed should be inverted in spirit: not "stop probing after two rounds", but **"a silent branch is not evidence of an incomplete task — re-probe before you ever consider adjudicating without a report, and read `no push since T` as *possibly finished*, not *possibly dead*."**

Everything downstream held: all four PRs are complete, CI-green, and were accepted on their merits. Zero work lost — which is this card's original claim, and it survived intact.
